prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments (2017)

Europe and Brexit
- A referendum on the final EU deal with the option to remain.
- Seek close alignment with the EU: retain single market and customs union benefits, protect freedom of movement, Erasmus+, citizens’ rights, policing and research cooperation, environmental and social standards.

Health and Social Care
- Immediate 1p on all Income Tax bands (and dividends) ringfenced for the NHS and social care; develop a dedicated health and care tax.
- Integrate health and social care, cap care costs, pooled local budgets by 2020, stronger support for carers.
- Workforce: end public sector pay cap, guarantee rights of EU staff, restore nurse bursaries, national workforce plan.
- Mental health parity: ringfenced funds, waiting time standards (e.g., six weeks for talking therapies; two weeks for first-episode psychosis), crisis care, end out-of-area placements, perinatal support, training for frontline services.
- Prevention: PrEP on the NHS; public health funding restored; obesity strategy, tobacco levy, minimum alcohol pricing (subject to legal outcome).

Education and Skills
- Nearly £7bn extra: protect per-pupil funding in real terms; fair national formula; protect and expand the Pupil Premium.
- Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium; raise workforce quality.
- Teachers: lift 1% pay cap; guarantee QTS; funded CPD; cut workload.
- Oppose new selective schools; strengthen local oversight; early SEND support.
- Curriculum: slim core incl. PSHE, SRE (consent, LGBT+ content), life skills; protect arts; better vocational routes and careers advice.
- Universities: restore maintenance grants; review finance (no retrospective changes); widen participation; protect EU links and research funds.
- Lifelong learning: expand apprenticeships, national colleges, adult learning accounts; address skills gaps; credit transfer system.

Economy and Tax
- Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; £100bn infrastructure plan (housing, schools, hospitals, transport, hyperfast broadband, renewables).
- Fair taxes: close avoidance, GAAR, reform corporation tax, review business rates (incl. Land Value Tax options); reverse several recent tax cuts benefiting higher incomes/wealth; raise NI threshold longer term.
- SMEs/entrepreneurs: expand British Business Bank; start-up allowance; scale-up mentoring; cut red tape uncertainty.
- Work and pay: promote a genuine living wage, transparency on pay ratios, strengthen gig-economy rights, curb zero-hours abuse, scrap tribunal fees.

Environment and Energy
- Five green laws; Zero-Carbon Britain (80% by 2040, net zero by 2050); 60% renewable electricity by 2030; back storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; maintain Euratom.
- Air quality: diesel scrappage; end sales of diesel cars/small vans by 2025; expand ULEZ; rapid shift of urban buses/private hire to low/zero emission.
- Homes: Green Buildings Act; at least 4m homes to EPC Band C by 2022; zero‑carbon standard for new builds.
- Nature: £2bn flood fund; legal natural capital targets; expand accessible green space; major tree planting; stronger animal welfare.
- Waste: Zero‑Waste Act; 70% recycling by 2022; extend food waste collections; 5p coffee cup charge; landfill/incineration tax reform.

Housing, Transport, Communities
- Build 300,000 homes/year by 2022, incl. 500,000 affordable; new garden cities; lift council borrowing caps; stronger affordable obligations; tackle land banking; community right of appeal.
- Renting: ban lettings fees; cap deposits; longer tenancies with fair rent rises; Rent to Own; Help to Rent; first refusal for sitting tenants; tackle rogue landlords; end rough sleeping with Housing First.
- Childcare and work: extra month’s paid paternity leave; day‑one flexible working; expand free childcare from 9 months for working parents, and all two‑year‑olds (long‑term aim: 30 hours).
- Transport: invest in rail (electrification, HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2), reopen/upgrade lines and stations, shift freight to rail, Young Person’s Bus Card (16–21), empower local bus franchising, rail ombudsman, cycling and walking.

Rights, Justice, Policing, Drugs
- Make all hate crimes aggravated offences; defend the Human Rights Act/ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; stronger FOI and media plurality rules.
- Policing: +£300m/year, end pay cap, body‑worn cameras, replace PCCs with elected boards.
- Justice: Victims’ Bill; presumption against short sentences; expand restorative justice; Women’s Justice Board; modernise courts; reverse excessive fees; protect legal aid access.
- Drugs: end imprisonment for possession for personal use; regulate cannabis for adults; move policy lead to Health; repeal the Psychoactive Substances Act.

Immigration and Asylum
- Efficient, fair system with entry/exit checks; annual skills debate; faster visas; remove students from migration stats; reinstate STEM post‑study visas; Migration Impact Fund; ESOL funding.
- Refugees: safe legal routes; 50,000 Syrian resettlements over the parliament; 3,000 unaccompanied children; 28‑day detention limit; allow work after six months; protect SOGI claimants.

International and Defence
- Support multilateralism (UN, NATO), 0.7% aid; tighter arms export controls; suspend sales to Saudi Arabia; conflict prevention and humanitarian leadership.
- Defence: spend 2% of GDP; cyber capability; minimum nuclear deterrent with three-boat posture; support veterans.

Constitution and Devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and English local elections; elected second chamber; cap donations at £10,000; stronger lobbying rules; weekend voting trials.
- Constitutional convention toward a federal UK; devolution on demand within England; protect Northern Ireland arrangements; fair funding with adjustments for Wales.
